A fall in the rate of inflation: prices still rise, but more slowly.
A sustained fall in the general price level (negative inflation).
A rise in aggregate demand faster than capacity: AD shifts to the right (low interest rates, tax cuts, higher spending, exports, credit).
A rise in firms' costs (wages above productivity, raw materials, fuel, imports after depreciation): SRAS shifts to the left.

front: Name four policies to reduce inflation.
back: Higher interest rates (monetary), higher taxes or lower spending (fiscal), supply-side policy, and wage and price controls.
